_source: AQA GCSE Design and Technology (8552) specification, section 2.2 Assessments and the NEA assessment criteria. Criterion NAMES and the 100-mark total are taken from AQA's published specification at https://www.aqa.org.uk/subjects/design-and-technology/gcse/design-and-technology-8552/specification/specification-at-a-glance
_note: The six assessment criteria for the NEA, and their mark allocation, are taken from the official AQA GCSE Design and Technology (8552) specification, Version 1.2 (6 June 2022), sections 4.4.4.1 to 4.4.4.6. The NEA is 100 marks (50% of the GCSE). Section 4.4.4 states that each band must be viewed HOLISTICALLY when marking, and that the criteria must not be viewed as a linear process.
_band_note: AQA marks by best fit within a band: work that fully meets a band is placed at the top of it, that mostly meets it in the middle, and that just meets it at the bottom.

criteria.name: Identifying and investigating design possibilities
criteria.description: Investigating the contextual challenge: identifying design possibilities, researching the client's and user's needs and wants, and investigating the work of others. AQA expects evidence of investigation, not description.
criteria.evidence: A top-band response identifies and investigates a range of design possibilities arising from the contextual challenge, with perceptive research into the needs, wants and values of the intended user, and clear evidence that investigating the work of others has informed the direction taken.

criteria.name: Producing a design brief and specification
criteria.description: Turning the investigation into a design brief and a specification that is objective and measurable, so the design work can be tested against it later.
criteria.evidence: A top-band response produces a clear design brief grounded in the investigation, and a detailed specification of measurable criteria which the design and the prototype can be evaluated against.

criteria.name: Generating design ideas
criteria.description: Generating a range of initial design ideas in response to the brief, showing creativity and an understanding of materials and processes.
criteria.evidence: A top-band response generates a range of creative initial ideas that clearly respond to the design brief, communicated with enough skill that a third party can understand them, and showing understanding of the materials and processes involved.

criteria.name: Developing design ideas
criteria.description: Iteratively developing ideas through modelling, testing and the views of others, with detail of materials, dimensions, finishes and production, so the design is ready to make.
criteria.evidence: A top-band response develops ideas iteratively, using modelling and testing to make and justify design decisions, and arrives at a detailed proposal giving materials, dimensions, finishes and production requirements that satisfies the specification.

criteria.name: Realising design ideas
criteria.description: Making the prototype: a logical sequence of production, selection of appropriate materials and components, safe and accurate use of tools and processes, and the quality of the finished outcome.
criteria.evidence: A top-band response shows a logical and achievable sequence of production, selects appropriate materials and components, works safely and accurately with specialist tools and processes, and produces a high-quality prototype that functions as intended.

criteria.name: Analysing and evaluating
criteria.description: Analysing and evaluating the design decisions and the finished prototype against the brief and specification, drawing conclusions and identifying how the outcome could be improved.
criteria.evidence: A top-band response critically analyses and evaluates the design decisions and the final prototype against the specification and the views of the user, draws appropriate conclusions, and identifies specific improvements with reference to measurable criteria.
